market.title: Donald Trump — Out as President Before 2027?
resolutionNote: Both platforms require an actual, permanent departure from office - resignation, conviction and removal following impeachment, or a sustained Twenty-Fifth Amendment Section 4 process (both Houses of Congress upholding the Vice President and Cabinet's determination of presidential inability by a two-thirds vote). A temporary Section 3 handover, an unconfirmed Section 4 invocation, or impeachment without removal do not count on either platform.
Kalshi's own wording: "If Donald Trump leaves office before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes."
One real gap between the platforms: Polymarket's tracked contract resolves by Dec 31, 2026, while Kalshi's resolves a day later, before Jan 1, 2027.

text: Despite recurring speculation, Trump remains firmly in office, and prediction markets price a departure before 2027 at just 5-6%.

The most serious formal push so far came in April, when Rep. Jamie Raskin introduced a bill, backed by 50 Democratic co-sponsors, to create a 17-member bipartisan commission to assess invoking the 25th Amendment over concerns about Trump's mental fitness. It has no realistic path through the Republican-controlled House.
The White House has repeatedly pushed back on fitness concerns, with Trump's physician describing him as being in "excellent health" and Trump himself claiming he has "aced" his cognitive exams.

Structural hurdles make removal unlikely regardless of the political noise: an impeachment conviction needs a two-thirds Senate supermajority, and a sustained 25th Amendment case requires both chambers of Congress to agree by that same threshold.
marketBrief.author: Owain Flanders
